questions.prompt: What is the safest way to learn a Ruby language feature?
options: Build a minimal example, predict the result, then test a boundary case.
Assume the feature handles all business validation automatically.
Skip checking the installed Ruby version.
Copy code into production without tests.
questions.answer_key: Build a minimal example, predict the result, then test a boundary case.
questions.explanation: Build a minimal example, predict the result, then test a boundary case. The other options either overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unsafe/unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: When should a Hash be preferred to an Array?
options: When no key/value relationship exists.
When values are naturally looked up by meaningful keys.
When duplicate values must be automatically removed.
When each item must always be stored in numeric sort order.
questions.answer_key: When values are naturally looked up by meaningful keys.
questions.explanation: When values are naturally looked up by meaningful keys. The other options either overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unsafe/unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of a small method with a clear contract?
options: It removes the need to validate input.
It always runs faster than inline code.
Its behavior is easier to explain, test, and reuse.
It makes runtime errors impossible.
questions.answer_key: Its behavior is easier to explain, test, and reuse.
questions.explanation: Its behavior is easier to explain, test, and reuse. The other options either overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unsafe/unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: What should guide a class public interface?
options: Expose all mutable state without checks.
Create inheritance for every relationship.
Store all application data in global variables.
The behavior callers need, with internal state kept consistent.
questions.answer_key: The behavior callers need, with internal state kept consistent.
questions.explanation: The behavior callers need, with internal state kept consistent. The other options either overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unsafe/unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: Why commit Gemfile.lock for an application?
options: To record the resolved dependency set for reproducible installs.
To replace application tests.
To keep all gems updated automatically.
To hide runtime errors from CI.
questions.answer_key: To record the resolved dependency set for reproducible installs.
questions.explanation: To record the resolved dependency set for reproducible installs. The other options either overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unsafe/unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: How should a program handle an expected parsing failure?
options: Retry forever with no delay or bound.
Rescue the specific expected exception and report a useful result.
Rescue Exception and silently continue every time.
Delete the input file after any exception.
questions.answer_key: Rescue the specific expected exception and report a useful result.
questions.explanation: Rescue the specific expected exception and report a useful result. The other options either overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unsafe/unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: How should untrusted values be inserted into SQL?
options: Base64-encode the value and treat it as trusted.
Remove all punctuation and assume the query is safe.
Use parameterized queries or prepared statements.
Interpolate the value directly into SQL text.
questions.answer_key: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements.
questions.explanation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements. The other options either overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unsafe/unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: How can shared mutable data be protected from concurrent updates?
options: Assume thread scheduling is always predictable.
Add sleeps until the race seems to disappear.
Disable all tests in concurrent code.
Use an appropriate synchronization or message-passing design.
questions.answer_key: Use an appropriate synchronization or message-passing design.
questions.explanation: Use an appropriate synchronization or message-passing design. The other options either overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unsafe/unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: What makes a deployment more reproducible?
options: Declare runtime and dependencies, configure through environment, and run checks.
Rely on undocumented local machine state.
Commit production credentials to source control.
Skip health checks after a release.
questions.answer_key: Declare runtime and dependencies, configure through environment, and run checks.
questions.explanation: Declare runtime and dependencies, configure through environment, and run checks. The other options either overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unsafe/unverified behavior.

options: Enable it without testing performance or compatibility.
Keep it optional, record version assumptions, and verify current release notes.
Require it for every beginner exercise.
Assume all Ruby implementations behave identically.
